title: etbb-july-2024-may-2025-update.pdf — section 173
text:
22. Where the focus of a hearing is to establish a litigant’s needs and how they will be managed,
the request for adjustments, together with any medical evidence provided, should then be
discussed with all the parties present during a case management hearing or, in the case of
criminal, family and certain other courts, a ground rules hearing.

23. It does not usually matter whether there is an entire hearing dedicated to discussing the
proposed adjustments or whether the discussion is part of a wider case management
discussion. What matters is that the subject is fully explored.
131

24. Once arrangements for the hearing are made, they are not set in stone. It may subsequently
become apparent that further adjustments are needed or that previously identified
adjustments are not needed. There are many reasons why needs change, including the
fluctuating effects of some disabilities.
